prompt.brief: Design a globally distributed market-data service that normalizes exchange feeds, serves fresh quotes over APIs and streams, and clearly communicates market status and price freshness.
successSignals: Define exchange feed adapters, symbol identity, quote/trade sequencing, corrections, trading sessions, entitlements, and freshness contracts.
Separate durable raw feeds and normalized events from hot latest-price projections, historical queries, and fan-out to subscribed clients.
Handle feed gaps, duplicate/out-of-order ticks, market halts, regional failover, connection churn, and millions of concurrent subscriptions.
Explain delayed-data labeling, replay, rate limits, auditability, observability, and degraded stale-quote behavior.

functional: Ingest authorized feeds from multiple exchanges, normalize quotes and trades, and expose latest prices, candles, and market status.
Support REST and WebSocket subscriptions with symbol entitlements, sequence/freshness metadata, reconnect replay, and throttling.
Persist raw and corrected events, rebuild projections after gaps, and audit feed transformations and customer access.
nonFunctional: Propagate an accepted feed update to subscribed clients within one second and serve latest-price reads with p95 under 100ms.
Scale to millions of concurrent subscriptions and bursty market opens without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 5M concurrent subscriptions and 100k normalized ticks per second
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Globally distributed market-data service commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Globally distributed market-data service writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Globally distributed market-data service version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Globally distributed market-data service by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Globally distributed market-data service work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Globally distributed market-data service projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Globally distributed market-data service projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Globally distributed market-data service records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Globally distributed market-data service latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
